races.name: www.mourneabbeyoil.ie Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beechingstoke
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Andrew Slattery and 7lb claimer Josh Younge; 65 days off the track, showed P-P over 2m on good ground so the trip and conditions are familiar, though no win yet from limited starts.

runners_data.name: Belladaball
runners_data.note: Cromwell and Donoghue combination is always worth noting — true hold-up mare with a win and a third on similar good ground in her record; will find herself closer than ideal in this traffic, which mutes her chance unless the pace is genuinely strong late.

runners_data.name: Easter Bonnet
runners_data.note: Mullins/Hayes combo, won on good ground over 2m and placed prominently, making her an ideal sit-just-off type; the 0 and 4 finishes are a concern but the profile fits a race where the front two tire.

runners_data.name: Emerald Enigma
runners_data.note: Perfect 2-from-2 on good ground, both at 2m, both ridden by Townend for Mullins — the standout class and experience angle in this race; 82 days since last run is worth watching but connections clearly have her ready.

runners_data.name: Flowing Fast
runners_data.note: Style unknown, lightly raced with an awkward recent form string including a fall and a pulled-up; amateur rider (7lb claimer Kennedy) and no clear going profile makes this an opaque runner to assess.

runners_data.name: Fraher Field
runners_data.note: Lower-rated at OR 104 and a true hold-up type who will be shuffled closer in this big field; best run was a second on good ground at 2m but the redistribution into midfield undercuts any finishing kick she might possess.

runners_data.name: Golden Wings
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends Jack Kennedy, but the horse fades in finishes and showed just one placed run in four on relevant going; the hold-up style is genuine but unsuited by the likely pace shape here.

runners_data.name: Jolly D'olivate
runners_data.note: Fades in finishes across her two relevant runs (8th and 9th on good ground) and the hold-up style combined with a recent run just 11 days ago raises condition questions; not well-placed for this pace shape.

runners_data.name: Kaleo Ametsa
runners_data.note: Six runs without a win, placed at 2m on good ground twice, and a genuine hold-up type who could get a run if the pace is true; however, the record suggests a horse that reaches a ceiling rather than wins.

runners_data.name: Kauto Empress
runners_data.note: Unknown style, lightly raced with just a 10th on good ground, amateur rider, and a fade warning — almost nothing positive in the data to project a competitive run here.

runners_data.name: Queenofqueenstreet
runners_data.note: 388 days off the track is a massive flag — one hurdles run (15th) is the entire record; the hold-up style and long absence make meaningful involvement very unlikely.

runners_data.name: The Orphan Girl
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained, flat form showed progression culminating in a win (4-3-4-1 sequence), lightly raced over hurdles and style unknown; the unknown factor cuts both ways and warrants a line at a price.

runners_data.name: Windy Grey
runners_data.note: Amateur rider, lightly raced, fades in finishes, and best run on hurdles track was an 8th on heavy ground — nothing in the data points to competitiveness on good going in a 20-runner maiden.

runners_data.name: Wonderful Everyday
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Mullins and Danny Mullins; her form suggests she makes the pace without always lasting (5-6-2-7-10 recent finishes), and a contested lead against Emerald Enigma risks burning her out before the last.

runners_data.name: Absolutley Fab
runners_data.note: Just four years old with a single 12th-place run on good ground to her name; a genuine hold-up type who will race closer than suited in this field, compounding the lack of form evidence for optimism.

runners_data.name: Kenny's Jewel
runners_data.note: Slevin in the saddle is a positive but fades in finishes and has three runs without threatening — the hold-up style is real but the form does not suggest she can exploit even a perfectly run race.

runners_data.name: Misty Valentine
runners_data.note: Only a pulled-up run to reference on good ground; unknown finishing position makes this a near-blank slate, and the hold-up profile offers little hope without demonstrated ability to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Neat As A Pin
runners_data.note: Bolger runner who unseated and then finished 12th — two runs, no encouragement, fades in finishes, and the 7lb claimer Lane adds little experience; hard to construct a case here.

runners_data.name: Thelittleredfox
runners_data.note: No jockey listed, 12th in only run on good ground, fades in finishes, unknown style — virtually no meaningful data to project any contribution to the finish.

runners_data.name: Sea Limit
runners_data.note: Unknown style and going preference, 113 days since last run, single sixth-place finish referenced — complete unknown who could surprise at a big price in a chaotic large-field maiden but profiles as a blind stab.

races.paceDynamic: Wonderful Everyday and Emerald Enigma are the two confirmed front-runners in a 20-runner maiden, and with both likely to press for the early lead, this race will be run at an honest, contested gallop from the outset — neither handler (both Mullins-trained) will want to concede the rail cheaply. Emerald Enigma brings a perfect 2-from-2 record on good ground and Paul Townend in the saddle, giving her the class edge at the sharp end, while Wonderful Everyday's record suggests she sets the pace without always lasting home. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Golden Wings, Belladaball, Absolutley Fab, and Fraher Field are genuine hold-up horses who will find themselves racing closer than ideal in a large field that compresses quickly on a jumping course. A genuine pace from the front on Good ground over 2m1f at Cork strongly favours resolute prominent racers and well-bred types with the stamina to capitalise once the pace-setters crack — hold-up horses shuffled forward out of role will not get the true late-run conditions they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Enigma Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Emerald Enigma leads or tracks Wonderful Everyday comfortably and the gallop is strong but not suicidal, setting up a test of quality and stamina.
scenarios.body: Townend can dictate or sit a length off the lead, rating the race perfectly, and Emerald Enigma's unbeaten record on good ground (2/2) points to her having the class to see it out; the contested pace softens Wonderful Everyday late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Wonderful Everyday and Emerald Enigma burn each other out and neither sees out the trip, a prominent racer sitting just off the heat inherits.
scenarios.body: Easter Bonnet, with form figures of 1-P-0-4 including a course win on good ground and Brian Hayes aboard for Mullins, is ideally positioned to pounce; Beechingstoke's P-P profile also suits a prominent run into a vacated lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Breach Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely fierce and the field string out, creating a true stamina test where a hold-up horse gets a clear run.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires hold-up types to get their natural position — possible for Belladaball (Cromwell/Donoghue, 3 good-ground runs, placed once) or Kaleo Ametsa if the pace is honest enough to bring them into it; the redistribution flags temper confidence significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Profits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large 20-runner field causes interference, fallers, or a muddled pace that scrambles the normal order entirely.
scenarios.body: An unknown type like The Orphan Girl (flat form of 4-3-4-1, lightly raced over hurdles, Fahey yard) or Sea Limit could surface in a chaotic finish that negates class and pace advantage; these scenarios are low probability but non-trivial in maiden hurdles of this size.

watchPoints.text: Watch Emerald Enigma's jumping under Townend — if she fluently leads or tracks Wonderful Everyday and jumps cleanly, she will be very hard to peg back given her unbeaten good-ground record.

Wonderful Everyday and Emerald Enigma head-to-head early: if they press each other hard from flag fall, both could be spent before the second-last, dramatically opening the race for Easter Bonnet or Beechingstoke sitting just behind.

With 20 runners in a mares maiden hurdle, interference and fallers at early flights are a genuine risk — horses like Flowing Fast (previous fall in form) and Neat As A Pin (unseated) carry jumping reliability concerns that could affect those around them.

Belladaball and Golden Wings will be racing closer than their natural style dictates — if either gets an awkward position or is hampered early, their hold-up instincts may cause them to drop away rather than improve through the field.

The Orphan Girl's flat form arc (progressive, winning) is worth monitoring if she settles — Fahey has a 1/14 strike rate in the 14-day window and the horse is lightly exposed over timber, making her a live each-way unknown in the chaos of a 20-runner field.

races.name: John O'Flynn Motors 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Arctic Flame
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with strong similar-going record (9 from 12 on Good), has won over this sort of trip at Cork recently and returns in solid form — needs a real gallop to close which may not materialise given the single pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Eastmore
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with an outstanding record on Good ground (14 from 15 similar-going starts) and five recent placings at the trip — Philip Byrnes keeps it straightforward and this horse's consistency from a handy position makes it the primary beneficiary of a moderate pace.

runners_data.name: Let's Go La Fichad
runners_data.note: The confirmed sole front-runner who won last time over further on Good; gets uncontested lead under Ricky Doyle, ran just seven days ago which may count against stamina reserves, but controls this entirely if jumping fluently — form on Good is limited to two runs (1W1P) which tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: In The Trenches
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from the Gavin Cromwell yard with an excellent similar-going record (13 from 15), won over 19f on Good recently and tackles this trip again with the young apprentice Eoin Staples; needs a more searching pace than this race shape is likely to produce.

runners_data.name: Gino Bella
runners_data.note: Prominent-running type wearing headgear, won on Good ground last time out for Patrick Foley and is effective around this sort of trip — the moderate pace suits horses travelling close to the leader, and this consistent mare ran just 24 days ago in good nick.

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott, prominent-racer with five recent runner-up finishes on Good ground who seems to find one or two too good; travels well and is ideally positioned for a moderate-pace race but the consistent second-placing record is a concern for winning.

runners_data.name: Quint Major
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form reads poorly (7th, 8th, 11th in three of last five) and who showed only one win in similar going conditions — moderate record and nothing in the data to suggest a bounce-back here.

runners_data.name: Metamorpheus
runners_data.note: Ran only two days ago which is a significant freshness flag; hold-up horse from the Andrew McNamara yard with two recent runner-up finishes on Good, sits in midfield through redistribution and could produce a late effort if the pace develops, though the quick turnaround is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Kilt
runners_data.note: An out-and-out hold-up horse by true profile — won over 17f on Good and has placed prominently — mapped to midfield here because the field is back-heavy; Shane O'Callaghan claims 3lb which helps the weight, but racing out of natural role at 0.91 style fit tempers the chance.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: Consistent on Good ground (12 from 12 similar-going runs) with a win and three places, but a natural rear-of-field type pushed forward in this compressed field through redistribution; J J Slevin is high class and can adapt, yet the 0.92 style fit signals this horse is unlikely to be in its comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Midnight Eagle
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, and redistribution places it in midfield rather than its natural rear position; showed a place two runs ago over 17f Good but the pattern of weakening late on combined with racing out of role makes this a difficult win case.

runners_data.name: Max Meridius
runners_data.note: Youngest-rated horse in the field (OR 93) and also flagged as a fader; Danny Mullins is an obvious asset but Max Meridius won over a much shorter 18f trip and the redistribution from its natural hold-up position, combined with the finishing tendency, stacks up against it here.

races.paceDynamic: Let's Go La Fichad is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse willing to lead, will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without any pressure from rival pace-setters — this is a single-setter race on Good ground over 2m1f at Cork. The prominent horses Eastmore, Gino Bella and Dairy Force will track closely behind, creating a compact early order, while the bulk of the field — Arctic Flame, In The Trenches, Metamorpheus and others — will fill midfield to rear. This moderate, uncontested tempo is the classic setup that rewards hold-up horses with a finishing kick, provided they can close the gap from a long way back on a track where Good ground allows that run, but it equally rewards the leading prominent horses who conserve energy and mount a challenge from a controlled position. Tactically, this race shape most favours the front-to-prominent profile — horses tracking the steady pace without exertion, poised to hit the front from the second-last — over true closers who need a strong gallop to make ground. Several runners including Kilt, Le Diablo, Midnight Eagle and Max Meridius are redistributed to midfield because the field holds more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear in a 12-runner field; of those, Kilt and Le Diablo are most capable of adapting, but none are operating in their ideal role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Go La Fichad sets a controlled tempo and the prominent trackers Eastmore, Gino Bella or Dairy Force sit close enough to pounce from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Let's Go La Fichad dictates a relaxed gallop, and the horses travelling smoothly just off his back have first run on the field entering the straight, never giving the closers enough of a pace gap to bridge. On Good ground at Cork, horses who travel prominently and stay organised over the hurdles have a decisive positional advantage when the tempo is this moderate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Go La Fichad is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and the prominent horses are slow to assert entering the straight.
scenarios.body: At a moderate pace, a front-runner can control the race entirely, conserve energy and find a second wind when the field tries to close — particularly if jockey Ricky Doyle times the challenge perfectly and the horse jumps fluently throughout. On Good ground the attrition is low enough to make this a live threat, and Let's Go La Fichad's recent course win over similar conditions gives this a real basis.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace lifts in the final mile creating enough of a true gallop for the closers to make meaningful ground from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Arctic Flame and In The Trenches, both genuine hold-up types with strong similar-going records, would be the primary beneficiaries if the race turns into a searching test, as both carry good recent form and experienced jockeys who can thread through a compressed field. However, the redistribution of several other nominal hold-up horses into midfield compresses the rear group, making this scenario harder to deliver — the true closers may find their late runs blunted by traffic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Attrition Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong through the middle section and the field strings out, with several prominent horses weakening at the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: A hidden increase in tempo would expose the less-seasoned prominent horses, rewarding runners like Metamorpheus or Le Diablo who settle smoothly in midfield and produce a measured late effort. This is the least likely shape given the lone front-runner and the absence of any confirmed pace pressure, but the redistribution of several hold-up types through the middle of the field could accidentally create a bunched, scrappy race that plays into opportunistic closers.

watchPoints.text: Eastmore — if Philip Byrnes secures a prominent position just off Let's Go La Fichad's pace through the early stages, this horse's exceptional record on Good ground (14/15) and consistent placed form at the trip makes it the single most dangerous winner in this race shape.

Arctic Flame — hold-up angles are compromised by a lone moderate pace-setter, but Simon Torrens is an experienced pilot and this horse has won over 20f Good recently; if it gets a clear run from the rear it could arrive with a dangerous late challenge.

Let's Go La Fichad — ran seven days ago and takes on the lead role again; if the horse shows any signs of fatigue jumping the second-last after an uncontested lead, prominent chasers will sweep past quickly on Good ground.

Metamorpheus — the two-day turnaround from its last run is unusually tight for a jumper and Andrew McNamara's yard has not run one in such a short window recently; monitor market moves as a significant drift would confirm the quick return is a concern.

Kilt and Le Diablo — both are naturally rear-of-field horses mapped to midfield by redistribution; if either drifts back to their instinctive position in the early stages they will face an even larger closing task than the pace shape already imposes.

races.name: Follow Us On Instagram Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Two Can Plan
runners_data.note: OR 97 top-weight but recent form reads P067P — badly out of form and failing to complete; 101 days off the track and tongue-tie added, needs to show he retains ability before handicapper gives him any credit here.

runners_data.name: Pirate Island
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who needs to come from off the pace, but at 8yo his Good-ground form over this trip is modest (0W0P in similar conditions); Sean Flanagan gives him experience but the controlled tempo is against him.

runners_data.name: Midnight Musical
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a worrying tendency to fade in the final stages; five-year-old beaten in recent 20f Good-ground starts, and the honest but slow pace here will not expose the leaders early enough to suit her style.

runners_data.name: Toon Town
runners_data.note: Most interesting prominent-closer in the field — won over 20f on Good and placed at Cork's trip before; Shane O'Callaghan (3lb claimer) keeps the weight low, and the course-distance form gives him strong positional credentials if he can slot in behind Eaglewood.

runners_data.name: Let It Settle
runners_data.note: Ran only 11 days ago and was sixth in a 16f contest, now stepping up to 21f; Phillip Enright a senior rider but the horse's form shows a second over 17f on Good, suggesting the step up could unlock more, though he is a natural hold-up type who needs the pace to collapse.

runners_data.name: Inchiquin Maid
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Soft/Standard and placed on Good ground before — genuine hold-up horse in terms of style, but pushed forward on the map by redistribution due to the overcrowded rear; John Shinnick rides, and the mare's best form came when ridden handier than her recent runs suggest.

runners_data.name: Mambo Du Large
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with only three runs under Rules and all three on Good ground, suggesting no going concern; lightly raced and still unexposed, but form figures of P706 are raw and Tom Kelly (7lb claimer) needs the horse to improve dramatically.

runners_data.name: Taketwotoone
runners_data.note: Has finished sixth or worse in recent starts and fades in the closing stages — his true preference is to be ridden from the rear, but redistribution places him in midfield where he will not produce his best; Mr T O'Connor (7lb claimer, trainer-rider combo) is an unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Saint Peregrine
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who is the most natural partner for Eaglewood at the head of affairs; T14 of 1/16 suggests trainer is not in the best form, and the horse's Good-ground record over 20f is poor (14/15 similar-going runs), yet positional access is a real tactical asset here.

runners_data.name: El Regalo
runners_data.note: Fades late and his Good-ground form over comparable trips is weak (10/15 in similar conditions); a natural hold-up runner placed into midfield by redistribution, his chance depends entirely on a tempo collapse that this race shape is unlikely to produce.

runners_data.name: Uptaurintop
runners_data.note: Placed third over 20f on Good ground recently and third over 16f on Heavy — has some form, but is a true closer whose natural rear position is unavailable in an 18-runner field; Alan O'Sullivan (5lb) rides.

runners_data.name: Tasmanian Girl
runners_data.note: Trainer Declan Queally has a live 14-day strike rate (2/7) which is worth noting, but the mare's form figures of 560-P9 are dire and her Good-ground record (13/15) is poor; tongue-tie worn, will be ridden from behind the pack having been redistributed from the rear.

runners_data.name: Crypto Crash
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and Good-ground form is weak (10/15); stepping up markedly in trip from recent 12f starts, and the redistribution from the rear into midfield compounds an already difficult ask for an OR 76 horse.

runners_data.name: Inches Away
runners_data.note: Five consecutive zeros in recent form and 0W0P in similar going across seven efforts — nothing in the data recommends this horse, and the 64-day absence plus the tough 18-runner field makes this a difficult proposition for Paul Cashman's charge.

runners_data.name: Chesterbaylad
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort over 16f on Good (2nd) recently and a fourth over 18f, so has some form in the book; Josh Williamson (5lb) assists on the weight, but the horse fades late and the trip extension to 21f is a query.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Good (1W in Good-ground form) and has placed twice more — has latent ability; last run was only 10 days ago and trainer James Barcoe has a 0/5 T14, yet the light weight (142lbs) and recent outing give him a fitness edge at least.

runners_data.name: Eaglewood
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who will control the tempo; OR 95, sim-going record of 1W2P in 10 Good-ground starts shows ability to perform on this surface, though the last run (14th over 17f) is concerning — if Eaglewood fails to run its race the entire scenario architecture collapses.

runners_data.name: Lady Victrix
runners_data.note: Fades in the final stages and ran only 11 days ago (finished 10th over 24f on Good); a natural hold-up type redistributed into midfield, with three consecutive losing runs and a modest sim-going record (3/5), Paul W Flynn's T14 of 3/20 is the only mildly positive angle.

races.paceDynamic: Eaglewood is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-horse field and looks set to dictate from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop — no other horse appears both willing and able to challenge for the lead early, meaning the pace will be controlled and honest rather than frenetic. Saint Peregrine is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely track Eaglewood in second or third, giving the leader a clean passage throughout. The bulk of the field — Toon Town, Let It Settle, Midnight Musical, Mambo Du Large, Pirate Island and others — will be hunting from midfield to rear, needing the pace to collapse late, which it may not do given how gently Eaglewood can dictate. This race shape strongly favours horses racing close to the pace or tracking the leader, as the controlled tempo will not produce the late collapse that pure hold-up horses require; front-two-and-prominent profiles are best placed. The field carries significantly more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Taketwotoone, Inchiquin Maid, Uptaurintop, Tasmanian Girl and several others are genuine closers who are unlikely to secure their natural position and will find themselves squeezed into a midfield cluster where they cannot fully express their style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eaglewood Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Eaglewood sets a sustainable, uncontested lead and the large hold-up pack cannot close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Eaglewood bowls along in front at a steady clip, with Saint Peregrine the only horse close enough to challenge, and the sheer number of hold-up runners unable to collectively peel off the pack fast enough to reel in the leader on Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Eaglewood's early control lures a prominent-tracking horse into a perfect position to pounce at the last.
scenarios.body: The honest but moderate gallop set by Eaglewood allows a close tracker to conserve energy through the race and produce a decisive jump at the final hurdle; horses sitting second or third in the early-to-mid stages are ideally placed as the front-runner ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves quicker than expected or Eaglewood makes a hurdle error, collapsing the advantage and inviting a late charge.
scenarios.body: A stumble or misjudgement from Eaglewood at a crucial flight disrupts the controlled tempo and the large group of hold-up horses — Pirate Island, Toon Town, Uptaurintop — close rapidly in the final two flights; this scenario is discounted because the closers are operating out of their natural position and True hold-up horses are congested in midfield.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Implodes — Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If carnage at hurdles, multiple fallers or interference breaks the race wide open and a lower-rated runner survives the chaos.
scenarios.body: In a field of 18 over hurdles the probability of interference or a multiple-runner pile-up at an early flight is non-trivial; a lightly-raced or fresh horse scrambling clear of trouble could benefit from a reduced field.

watchPoints.text: Eaglewood is the critical pace-setter — any hurdle error or stumble from this horse destroys the controlled tempo and reshuffles the entire race shape dramatically with 18 runners behind.

The redistribution cluster of Taketwotoone, Inchiquin Maid, Uptaurintop, Tasmanian Girl and others will be squeezed into a tight midfield group — watch for interference, crowding and horses being hampered at the early flights in an 18-runner handicap hurdle.

Toon Town's OR 91 combined with Good-ground course form and a 3lb claimer makes him the most dangerous prominent-tracking profile — if Saint Peregrine cannot hold second and Toon Town slots in behind Eaglewood early, he becomes the dominant each-way threat.

Saint Peregrine's trainer T14 of 1/16 is a weak flow, and the horse's sim-going record (14/15) is poor — despite the natural positional advantage of a prominent runner in this shape, class and form queries mean he should not be automatically trusted to fulfil the role.

Surviving Murmansk ran just 10 days ago and carries the lowest weight in the field (142lbs) — fresh legs and light burden in a messy 18-runner handicap can always spring a surprise, particularly if chaos at the hurdles reduces the effective competition mid-race.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beyond Forgiveness
runners_data.note: Unknown style, 456 days off the track is a serious concern for a maiden hurdle; trainer Kelly has 0/5 in the 14-day window and this lightly-raced five-year-old faces a stiff fitness test on return.|

runners_data.name: Buachaill Jagoes
runners_data.note: Six-year-old maiden with only a distant flat fourth on record, 141 days absent, and trainer O'Brien 0/4 in the window — negligible evidence to work with and profile screams of inexperience.|

runners_data.name: Carajillo
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse by profile who showed some ability on Good ground previously; with several genuine closers in the field, it is unlikely to secure its preferred rear position and may race closer to midfield than ideal, blunting its effectiveness.|

runners_data.name: Eye Contact
runners_data.note: Returned just 13 days ago and has headgear (tongue-tie, blinds) in play; a genuine closer who placed once in ten similar-going runs, but racing out of its natural deep position in this crowded rear, and the fading pattern is a worry.|

runners_data.name: Lastofthenatives
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with an ugly recent form string including three pulls-up; has run twice on similar going without trouble but the P0 latest two are hard to ignore for any positive case.|

runners_data.name: Livio
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner from the powerful Mullins yard, which has 11 winners from 54 in the 14-day window; ran a creditable third over 2m4f on Good last time and the drop in trip with a clear lead to exploit is a significant tactical advantage in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Sankofa
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced and unknown in style; one third on debut is the entire picture, and 120 days off the track and the Kelly stable's current 0/5 form makes this very speculative.|

runners_data.name: The Monkey Pole
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has run six times on similar going, placing twice; a genuine hold-up performer by profile who is most likely to actually secure a rear position in this field and has a real chance if the pace scenario produces a late opportunity.|

runners_data.name: Vargas
runners_data.note: Elliott-trained with 2/41 in the 14-day window, but a 239-day layoff and a career form reading of P/P- means significant fitness and ability questions remain unanswered before a debut over hurdles here.|

runners_data.name: Woodie Wiley
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has run twice on Good going without threatening but at least stays the course; the 30-day gap is manageable but the form figures are unencouraging.|

runners_data.name: Adifferentballowax
runners_data.note: Elliott's four-year-old has been prominent in his runs but posted three consecutive 9ths on Good ground, so the style fits this race shape but the ability level is firmly in question.|

runners_data.name: Bury Your Past
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old unknown in style with a hurdles pull-up and a flat fifth in the book; trainer Gearoid O'Loughlin has 0/0 in the 14-day window and the profile is too thin to assess confidently.|

runners_data.name: Devine Genius
runners_data.note: A genuinely poor recent flat record — five runs, worst finish tenth, predominantly at shorter trips — means this is a hold-up horse being asked to step up markedly in trip over hurdles, racing in a position further forward than natural; the form base offers very limited confidence.|

runners_data.name: Johnny Rambo

races.paceDynamic: Livio is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field and, critically, faces no identified rival willing or able to press him hard for the lead, meaning he should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good ground over 2m2f at Cork. Johnny Rambo and Adifferentballowax are the clearest prominent challengers and will look to sit just behind Livio, creating a race that flows at an even tempo rather than a pressured, attritional one — conditions that typically reward horses who can travel prominently and kick from the front rather than those making up ground from deep. The field carries a substantial cluster of genuine hold-up horses — Devine Genius, Carajillo, The Monkey Pole, Eye Contact, Lastofthenatives, and others — but the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear, and the most likely to genuinely secure their natural position are The Monkey Pole, Master Sydney, and Woodie Wiley, while several others will be caught in mid-division traffic without the gaps they need. This race shape — one unhurried front-runner, a sustainable pace, and a compressed midfield — strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and produce their effort from the second-last hurdle, disadvantaging true hold-up types who need a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Livio controls, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Livio sets a comfortable, uncontested pace and the race is decided by who can attack from the front two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Livio dictates every yard at a fair clip, and the horses tracking him — Johnny Rambo and Saporetti — find the relatively sedate tempo playing directly to their strengths, allowing them to quicken at the business end without having burned surplus energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace drifts, late energy counts
scenarios.trigger: If Livio sets an unusually slow early pace that compresses the entire field and produces a sprint finish off the last hurdle.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow early tempo means even genuine hold-up horses get into a good rhythm and have something left to unleash late, with a scramble developing from the second-last as the field fans wide.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent horse outstays field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to stretch the field but Livio or a tracking rival simply stays on strongest up the straight.
scenarios.body: A steady but genuine gallop exposes the stamina limitations of hold-up horses coming from off the pace on Good ground, and a horse sitting second or third travelling well into the straight wins with ears pricked.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider from midfield pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace scenario produces a compressed, slowly-run race that leaves midfield horses completely untroubled and one unexposed runner produces a big move.
scenarios.body: An unknown quality in this field — Majestic Horizon, Sankofa, or Vargas — has its lightly-raced profile masked by the undemanding gallop and produces a late challenge that the market has underestimated.

watchPoints.text: Livio (Mullins, Cleary-Farrell) is the only confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field — if he slots in unchallenged on Good ground he controls every aspect of this race and his rivals' fates depend entirely on the pace he sets.

Johnny Rambo's two wins both came over 2m on Good ground — watch whether he can get his prominent pitch in a 21-runner field early on, because a clean passage just off the leader is essential to his profile working here.

The cluster of hold-up horses — Devine Genius, Carajillo, Eye Contact, and Lastofthenatives — who are mapped to midfield rather than their natural position at the rear creates a congestion risk in the early stages that could cost several runners any chance.

Master Sydney and The Monkey Pole are the genuine hold-up horses most likely to actually secure a position at the rear; if the pace scenario produces a late sprint, watch which of this pair gets the cleaner passage to the outside turning for home.

Le Vent d'Ex, Champagne Diamond, and Majestic Horizon all have no jockey declared — confirm market moves closer to post time, as any well-backed debutant or returning runner in this open maiden carries outsider threat.

races.paceDynamic: Jupiter Du Gite is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 21-runner field and, assigned to a reserve jockey, will be allowed to bowl along at a measured, uncontested gallop on Good ground over 2m2f at Cork — a scenario that hands him full control of the tempo. With Palace Boy, Miners Bridge, Inthenickoftime, Crowsatedappletart, Certamen and Diamond Tipp all prominent types, there is a meaningful cluster of horses wanting to race close to the pace, which should string the field out early but won't seriously pressurise Jupiter Du Gite's lead. The field carries more prominent and hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate cleanly — Katherine, Imperial Miss, Alentejo, Boola Times, Dictionary Corner, Scathach and Ballyminnion Boy are genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is already oversubscribed, meaning they are unlikely to find the ground-saving, late-finishing positions they prefer. A steady-to-fair gallop set by one uncontested leader on Good turf at an end-of-card spot strongly favours prominent racers who can track close to the pace, conserve energy and quicken from two out — this race shape is tailor-made for hold-and-pounce prominent types rather than true closers being shuffled back further than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Jupiter Du Gite sets a fair but uncontested gallop and the prominent pack tracks him efficiently into the straight.
scenarios.body: Jupiter Du Gite controls fractions, the prominent cluster — Crowsatedappletart, Inthenickoftime, Miners Bridge — sit a length or two off the pace and are perfectly placed when the tempo lifts at the second-last; Good ground rewards those with the racing room to quicken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies Field
scenarios.trigger: If Jupiter Du Gite, unchallenged and well-weighted at OR 113, simply sets a tempo the field can never quite match and kicks clear from three out.
scenarios.body: With 21 runners and no one willing to commit early, Jupiter Du Gite builds an unassailable break; Good ground and a flat Cork finish mean he doesn't need much in reserve, and the reserve jockey has no pressure to do anything adventurous.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners burn too much fuel jostling for position in a 21-runner field and the early gallop proves more pressured than expected.
scenarios.body: A faster early clip in a big field causes the prominent group to fade from two out, creating a clear run for the better-handicapped hold-up types arriving with momentum; O'Grady Cracker and Boola Times, despite redistribution concerns, have shown ability to produce late efforts when the pace is genuine.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops at an even tempo and a handful of midfield-tracking types find daylight at the top of the straight in a chaotic 21-runner cavalry charge.
scenarios.body: With runners spread wide across Cork's track, horses sitting mid-division like Earl Neigh or Champagne Dawn could navigate clear where prominent runners are crowded; the scenario is plausible only if traffic patterns fall perfectly.

watchPoints.text: Jupiter Du Gite (Reserve 3 jockey) — watch whether the jockey establishes the lead cleanly or lets the 21-runner field crowd him early; if he gets away cleanly and unchallenged, the whole race shape shifts in favour of prominent types.

Crowsatedappletart — watch how Luke Burke Ott (7lb claimer) positions him in a 21-runner field; this horse won last time and suits a steady gallop, but getting caught wide on the first bend at Cork in a big field could undo his chance before it starts.

O'Grady Cracker — the ⚠ fade flag combined with a 10-day turnaround means J J Slevin must manage him carefully; watch whether he's ridden conservatively or committed early, as the former gives him a chance and the latter is likely to see him empty late.

Imperial Miss — ran just 1 day ago and will be navigating a crowded 21-runner field from further back than her natural position suggests; watch whether she shows any signs of freshness or is clearly running on fumes from a race 24 hours prior.

Miners Bridge — 398 days off the track is a long absence; watch in the parade ring for any signs of condition or fitness before concluding his strong Good-ground profile translates to a competitive first run back.
